name: Drawdown Control
rationale: Drawdown-control rules test explicit risk objectives instead of defaulting to total-return competition.
expected_benefit: Lower peak-to-trough losses with transparent return-retention trade-offs.
failure_modes: Can exit after most of the damage is done.
Can miss rebounds and permanently lag.
Can become a curve-fit risk overlay.

canonical_variants.name: Volatility-target drawdown overlay
canonical_variants.description: Scale exposure with a volatility target to reduce drawdown severity.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A volatility-target drawdown overlay may reduce maximum drawdown while retaining more growth than binary cash exits.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Reduce max drawdown by at least 25% relative while retaining at least 75% of benchmark CAGR.

canonical_variants.name: Equity-curve stop
canonical_variants.description: Stop trading after the strategy equity curve breaches a drawdown threshold.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: An equity-curve stop may prevent strategy degradation from compounding after a deep drawdown.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Reduce strategy max drawdown without materially lowering CAGR.

canonical_variants.name: Cooldown after loss
canonical_variants.description: Pause new entries after a realized loss or drawdown event.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A cooldown after loss may reduce whipsaw clustering in rule-based strategies.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Improve Sharpe without failing return retention below 70% of benchmark CAGR.

suggested_validation: Prespecify the risk objective before running.
Use date windows with major drawdowns and strong rebounds.
Do not stack multiple overlays until one simple overlay is understood.
execution_notes: Volatility-target overlays are executable. Equity-curve stops and cooldown rules are not implemented.
